sections.h2: GST 2.0 still runs four effective rates, not two

chart.title: Four effective rates and three narrow carve-outs remain after GST 2.0
chart.source: Gazette of India, Notification No. 9/2025-Central Tax (Rate), 17 September 2025.

sections.means: The four effective rates of 0%, 5%, 18% and 40% sit alongside three narrower carve-outs at 3%, 0.25% and 1.5%.
sections.todo: Treat any claim that India has moved to two rates as inaccurate until these categories are merged.

sections.h2: India's 2015 committee found a 15-15.5% neutral rate, then proposed tiers

chart.title: The 2015 committee's neutral rate was 15-15.5%, but it proposed tiers instead
chart.sub: Rates the 2015 committee calculated or proposed, %.

sections.means: The committee's single neutral rate was lower than the tiers it actually recommended for most goods.
sections.todo: Judge any single-rate proposal against the 2015 tiered design, which was built to avoid taxing a poor household's food and a rich household's luxury car at the same rate.

sections.h2: Singapore, the UAE and New Zealand still have standard rates of 5-15%

chart.title: The 'flat rate' countries each set a standard rate from 5% to 15%, with carve-outs
chart.source: Comparison table in the post, from national tax authorities.

sections.means: Each system in the table has one standard positive rate, but each also exempts or zero-rates a defined set of goods and services.
sections.todo: Compare any proposed single rate with these countries' carve-outs, not only their headline rates.
